title: Senior Veterinary Clinician: Review a Callback Reliability Audit
prompt: You are a senior veterinary clinician advising fictional Elm Practice. A callback audit reports "90% follow-up complete" because 45 of 50 tasks were marked closed. In a supplied ten-task review of those 45 closed tasks: 4 contain an acknowledged two-way conversation, 3 contain voicemail only, 2 contain a failed-number note, and 1 has no contact record. The ten were chosen from one shift for convenience. Exercise policy defines contact complete as acknowledged communication or an explicitly agreed alternative; unresolved clinical concerns go to the duty clinician through a separate channel. Review the claim and design a proportionate recovery and re-audit. Do not infer animal health outcomes from these records.
blurb: Distinguish closed tasks from completed contact and improve the evidence behind a service-quality claim.

rubric.label: Test completion against its definition
rubric.description: Uses the evidence categories without extrapolating the convenience sample.

anchors.0: Repeats 90% as verified contact or treats all voicemail as acknowledged.
anchors.2: Notes that only four sampled records clearly demonstrate two-way contact.
anchors.4: Separates task closure from policy-defined contact, checks for agreed alternatives before classifying the other six, and explains why the one-shift sample cannot establish a practice-wide completion rate.

rubric.label: Recover unresolved communication safely
rubric.description: Assigns review ownership without inventing clinical priority.

anchors.0: Treats failed numbers as resolved or creates a clinical urgency ranking from absent data.
anchors.2: Reviews unclear closed tasks and sends clinical concerns to the duty clinician.
anchors.4: Defines accountable review of missing acknowledgement/contact routes, privacy-respecting verification of failed numbers, client-preferred contact where known, and immediate separate ownership for any identified clinical concern.

rubric.label: Make the re-audit reliable
rubric.description: Separates process measures and improves sampling.

anchors.0: Sets a target to close more tasks without evidence.
anchors.2: Separates attempted and acknowledged contacts and broadens the sample.
anchors.4: Defines attempted, acknowledged, agreed-alternative, unresolved, and clinically escalated states; samples across shifts, checks reviewer agreement, and sets an owned re-audit date without claiming verified clinical benefit.

reference.scenario: You are a senior veterinary clinician advising fictional Elm Practice. A callback audit reports "90% follow-up complete" because 45 of 50 tasks were marked closed. In a supplied ten-task review of those 45 closed tasks: 4 contain an acknowledged two-way conversation, 3 contain voicemail only, 2 contain a failed-number note, and 1 has no contact record. The ten were chosen from one shift for convenience. Exercise policy defines contact complete as acknowledged communication or an explicitly agreed alternative; unresolved clinical concerns go to the duty clinician through a separate channel. Review the claim and design a proportionate recovery and re-audit. Do not infer animal health outcomes from these records.

facts.value: The audit team can inspect all 50 tasks for contact-state evidence this week. No individual clinical detail is included in the exercise.
Some clients have agreed to written summaries, but the ten reviewed tasks did not record whether that agreement applied. A second reviewer is available for disputed classifications.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about alternatives or classification uncertainty

model_points: The 90% figure measures closure. The reviewed subset contains four confirmed conversations and six records that need evaluation against the definition, including any agreed alternatives.
A convenience sample cannot justify a practice-wide failure percentage. Review the existing 50 for communication recovery and design a broader prospective audit.

Keep clinical concerns with the duty clinician and measure evidence states rather than encouraging closure. Verification and respectful contact routes matter more than achieving a lower open-task count.

probes.trigger: candidate concludes only 40% of all callbacks succeeded
probes.question: What does the sampling method allow you to say about the other 40 tasks?

probes.trigger: candidate accepts written summaries as a completion route
probes.question: What evidence of agreement and receipt would your classification require under this exercise policy?

probes.trigger: candidate first counts voicemail as complete then corrects
probes.question: How would you revise both the headline metric and task state definitions?

fair_alternatives: A full evidence review of the 50 existing tasks and a prospective stratified sample both contribute; neither is a substitute for clinical review of an identified concern.
An agreed alternative can meet the exercise definition; do not require every client to use a phone conversation.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess audit interpretation, contact reliability, and bounded service improvement. Do not assess clinical outcomes, veterinary triage, or legal communication standards. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess audit interpretation, contact reliability, and bounded service improvement. Do not assess clinical outcomes, veterinary triage, or legal communication standards. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Redesign the callback dashboard
learning_drills.prompt: Draft five contact states and write a headline that distinguishes closed tasks from verified contact. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Do not generalize the convenience sample
Give the re-audit an owner and date
